paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. The centurion, an army officer, could have said, "Jesus, get over here, I'm important." Instead he says, "I am not worthy to have You come under my roof." That's a man who knows exactly who he is and exactly Who he's talking to (Luke 7:6).

Then he asks for the simplest thing in the world: "But just say the word, and my servant will be healed." He doesn't need a show, a big house call or a long ceremony. He lives under authority every day, so he knows what happens when the right voice gives an order (Luke 7:7-8). He trusts that Jesus' word is enough all by itself, and Jesus marvels and says, "I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith" (Luke 7:9).

So what does that mean for you, baker? Faith isn't about being impressive or having the best reference letter. It's about knowing who Jesus is and trusting what He says, even when you can't see Him standing in your kitchen. I've been the stamper nobody picked up for years, and I'm telling you, the word of Jesus is enough, and when the messengers got back, the servant was in good health (Luke 7:10).
